slug: 2026-02-01 SITA and the Paradox of Centralized ICT Procurement in South Africas Public Sector
note: Study of SITA's statutory centralised ICT procurement; states no staff-run, agency-hosted, in-house-built or cadre fact.

facts.fact: SITA is stated to be tendering on behalf of SAPS and the Department of Water and Sanitation, and to use a backup solution so that a client's servers are serviced and maintained.
facts.system: SITA client server backup and maintenance

facts.fact: The Road Accident Fund seeks a service provider for end-to-end monitoring, detection and response on its existing in-house Microsoft Sentinel threat-detection solution (five years).
facts.system: Microsoft Sentinel TDR solution (Road Accident Fund)

facts.fact: SITA is inviting bids for a provider to architect, design, develop and test an incident management solution for SAPS, which has no single integrated system and runs outdated platforms (36 months).
The Electoral Commission's ICT department is stated to run its ICT environment, on VMware as the core virtualisation platform, for which it seeks licence renewal.
The Electoral Commission's public mobile app was originally built in-house for the 2019 elections, with updates in 2021 and 2024; the date is the original go-live year, outside the three-year window.
The Electoral Commission is re-advertising for redevelopment of its mobile app, saying the framework is outdated and insecure.

SITA is inviting bids for maintenance and support of the server hardware for its OSIS and NMS environments, the latter used to manage network service delivery to its clients, and for VPN software for the Free State Office of the Premier.

systems.country_label: Free State Office of the Premier
systems.owner: Free State Office of the Premier

note: Procurement report; 'in-house server-based' is a supplied, on-premises system bought from a contractor, not built or run by municipal staff.
Names South Africa only as one of several countries with Huawei-built data centres; no government staff, agency, in-house build or cadre fact.

facts.fact: The communications minister's written reply to Parliament states the State IT Agency (SITA) delivered 117 e-services through 35 digital products to more than 30 government departments and public entities in 2025/26; the reply gives no date, published 2026-10-05.

note: Passages state SITA's past failure to produce a common system and vendor-sourced storage; no named government system run, built or outsourced by a named body.
SITA leadership and mandate statements and an executive appointment; no system run, built or outsourced is stated, and SITA's shared-platform role is stated as intent only.
Interview about SITA's reputation and plans for multi-department platforms; no named system run, built or outsourced, and plans are intent only.
Passages are the speech's opening and conference background (GovTech hosted by SITA since 2006); no government-run or built system stated.

facts.fact: ITWeb describes SITA, an entity of the Department of Communications and Digital Technologies, as responsible for developing, operating and/or maintaining ICT services consumed by government departments, supporting over 100 departments and public entities including the police and defence (date is the publication date).

note: Rest is SITA executive recruitment and PSC findings; recruitment is not a fact.

slug: 2026-07-07 South Africa's state IT agency is slowing government tech rollout

facts.fact: TechCabal reports the minister calling SITA the state's central ICT engine, with departments waiting on it for the systems they need, and the PSC describing it as a central ICT procurement and service-delivery entity (date is the publication date).

note: Mostly governance and procurement failures of SITA; no named system or go-live.

facts.fact: The Citizen quotes the Public Service Commission chair describing SITA as an institution with a near monopoly of controlling IT services for the public service, and the minister calling it a key enabler of South Africa's ICT needs.

note: Mostly irregular expenditure and procurement findings; no named system or go-live.

facts.fact: SITA's 2024/25 annual report states the State Information Technology Agency, wholly owned by government, provides information technology, information systems and related services to national, provincial and local government departments as their agent, and records R2.06 billion owed by national departments for ICT services and products at 31 March 2025.

note: Only the agency fact is stated; no named system is stated as run or built by government staff, and the deeds system is a contractor's software development.

facts.fact: The SITA directors' report for the year ended 31 March 2024 states the company's business is providing information technology, information systems and related services to or on behalf of national, provincial and local government departments, as an agent of the South African Government.
The reply says the national EMR for PHC was developed in-house by the Department of Health, with no procurement adjudication.
facts.system: National Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system for PHC

note: Only a general claim that skilled engineers left government and procurement failed; no named body or system stated.

facts.fact: The minister says SITA developed the National e-Government Portal and will keep 98% core network availability for 7,570 connected government sites across national and provincial departments in 2024/25.

note: Nothing on government technical staff.
SITA named only as SA Connect partner; no system it runs or builds is stated.

facts.fact: The Department of Home Affairs says in a written reply that its civic-records digitisation programme is managed in-house under the Operations Branch and performed by departmental officials and interns, with no foreign company contracted.

note: SITA is named only as a partner in a contract run by Liquid; no systems run by government staff are stated.

facts.fact: The Western Cape Government says its Department of the Premier's Centre for e-Innovation created the Social Work Integrated Management System for the Department of Social Development.

The Western Cape Government says SWIMS, created by its Department of the Premier's Centre for e-Innovation with the Department of Social Development, went live in April 2024 and is used by 1,054 practitioners, at a cost of R6 million.

systems.owner: Western Cape Department of Social Development

note: Provincial government in the Western Cape; who runs and maintains SWIMS after launch is not stated.

facts.fact: The State Information Technology Agency (SITA), a government-owned organisation, provides IT services to public sector bodies and runs Home Affairs on IBM System Z mainframes.
The Department of Home Affairs says SITA technicians and engineers were attending to a fault on the SITA mainframe that affects access to the National Population Register.

note: Pan-African feature; nothing stated for South Africa on this question.

facts.fact: Home Affairs Minister Leon Schreiber thanked the department's in-house team of developers who built the Trusted Tour Operator Scheme (TTOS) digital platform.
The Home Affairs TTOS digital platform, built by the department's in-house developers in under six months, went live at 8am on 12 February 2025.
The Minister said the TTOS platform was built by Home Affairs' in-house team of developers, with no contractor named.

note: An in-house-developed ecosystem is mentioned with no named system, and legacy systems are under support contracts.

facts.fact: In a parliamentary reply the Department of Home Affairs said it continues to rely on the State Information Technology Agency (SITA) for critical legacy platforms and has not decided to leave it.
Minister Schreiber said the Trusted Tour Operator Scheme visa portal was built in-house by Home Affairs' own software development team.

Statistics SA's Statistician-General said in a reply signed 11 November 2024 that under the SITA Act the State Information Technology Agency must provide national and provincial departments with a private telecoms network and transversal and department-specific information systems (Persal, BAS, LOGIS), and data processing for them.
